guardian.title: Spain to introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy
guardian.description:
Move comes in response to Rome imposing similar measures after mass migration rush to Ceuta

Spain has announced it will introduce temporary border checks on visitors from Italy in response to Rome imposing similar measures after a mass rush of people from Morocco into Ceuta.

The checks, which come “amid the persistent irregular migration pressure” facing Italy, will start at midnight on Saturday and last until 7 September, Spain’s interior ministry said in a statement.

lemonde.description: L’association a porté plainte pour des soupçons de détournement de fonds publics et d’emploi fictif, après la publication d’un article du « Canard enchaîné ».

lemonde.title: Fragilisés par les aléas climatiques et les difficultés budgétaires, des festivals musicaux diversifient leurs activités pour tenir
lemonde.description: Marsatac, Cabaret Vert, Panorama, Au Foin de la rue, Ecaussystème… De plus en plus de festivals investissent des lieux à l’année ou développent d’autres services afin de s’ancrer davantage dans leur territoire et dégager d’autres ressources financières.

france24fr.title: Vietnam : face au dérèglement climatique, les Hmong en première ligne
france24fr.description: Dans les montagnes du nord du Vietnam, les Hmong, un peuple autochtone d'agriculteurs, vivent au rythme de la nature depuis des siècles. Augmentation des températures, pluies imprévisibles, glissements de terrain : ils se retrouvent aujourd'hui en première ligne face au dérèglement climatique.

france24fr.title: L'Arabie saoudite, le Pakistan et la Turquie concluent un pacte de défense
france24fr.description: Un pacte de défense a été signé vendredi par l'Arabie saoudite, le Pakistan et la Turquie, sur fond de tensions liées à la guerre au Moyen-Orient. Selon les experts, cette annonce envoie un message à l'Iran mais aussi aux États-Unis, perçus comme un partenaire de moins en moins fiable.

france24fr.title: Au moins 3 morts dans de nouvelles frappes russes sur la région de Kiev
france24fr.description: De nouvelles frappes russes ont fait au moins trois morts et sept blessés dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi à Kiev et dans sa région, alors que la défense antiaérienne ukrainienne peine à intercepter les missiles russes faute de munitions suffisantes.

france24fr.title: À Téhéran, le régime raconte sa guerre sur les murs de la ville (2/2)
france24fr.description: Téhéran dans la guerre (2/2). En Iran, la guerre passe aussi par les images. Dans la capitale, d'immenses affiches de propagande transforment les murs en vitrine du récit officiel, et sont conçues pour porter la voix du gouvernement bien au-delà des frontières. France 24 revient sur cette stratégie visuelle, façonnée depuis la Révolution islamique et désormais dopée par l'intelligence artificielle.

france24fr.title: Ukraine en direct : au moins quatre morts dans de nouvelles frappes russes sur la région de Kiev
france24fr.description: De nouvelles frappes russes ont fait au moins quatre morts et sept blessés dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi à Kiev et dans sa région, alors que la défense antiaérienne ukrainienne peine à intercepter les missiles russes faute de munitions suffisantes. ⁠L'armée ukrainienne a frappé les raffineries de pétrole russes d'Ilsky et de Syzran lors d'⁠attaques menées pendant la nuit. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Candidat à la présidentielle, Gabriel Attal porte plainte pour "ingérence étrangère" en provenance de la Russie
france24fr.description: L'ex-premier ministre et candidat à l'élection présidentielle de 2027 Gabriel Attal a porté plainte hier pour "ingérence étrangère" après la diffusion de "deepfakes" ou encore de "fausses unes de journaux" et de "fausses unes de journaux" en "provenance de réseaux russes".

france24fr.title: L'Espagne riposte face à Rome en imposant des contrôles aux frontières aux voyageurs venant d'Italie
france24fr.description: L'Espagne a décidé vendredi d'instaurer des contrôles temporaires aux frontières à ses ports et aéroports pour les voyageurs en provenance d'Italie. Madrid avait prévenu que de telles mesures de rétorsion seraient prises si Rome ne levait pas la suspension de l'accord de libre circulation de Schengen instaurée à la suite de l'afflux massif de migrants dans l'enclave espagnole de Ceuta.

france24fr.title: Le rappeur Dip Doundou Guiss invité de France 24
france24fr.description: Il est la voix d’une génération. Dip Doundou Guiss, le rappeur numéro un du Sénégal, est à Paris pour son concert au Cabaret Sauvage. Il présente à France 24 son nouveau single Ñogmante, sorti le 26 juin.

france24fr.title: Exclusif : l'ONU renouvelle son contrat avec Palantir malgré des craintes soulevées dans un audit
france24fr.description: Le Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM) s’apprête à renouveler pour cinq ans son contrat avec l’entreprise américaine de logiciels Palantir, malgré des "préoccupations majeures en matière de protection de la vie privée" soulevées dans un audit interne de 2025. Consulté par PassBlue et France 24, le document révèle les réticences de l’ONU à l'idée de confier à Palantir le traitement de données pour organiser la chaîne logistique de l'aide humanitaire.

france24fr.title: Pollution aux Pfas : la métropole de Rouen porte plainte contre BASF pour ses rejets dans la Seine
france24fr.description: La métropole Rouen Normandie a déposé plainte contre l'entreprise BASF pour ses rejets "massifs" dans la Seine de polluants éternels, en l'occurrence le TFA, a-t-elle annoncé vendredi. Une plainte qui concerne l'usine de Saint-Aubin-lès-Elbeuf, classée Seveso seuil haut, qui produit notamment le Fipronil, un insecticide interdit en Europe mais exporté vers le Brésil.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Var : le feu du Gros Bessillon fixé après 18 jours de mobilisation
Le feu du Gros Bessillon, dans le Var, fixé après 18 jours de mobilisation
france24fr.description: Le feu qui s'était déclaré fin juillet dans le massif du Gros Bessillon, dans le centre Var, est "fixé" après deux semaines et demie de mobilisation des pompiers, a annoncé vendredi la préfecture.

france24fr.title: "Tout est sec" : le monde du vin victime du dérèglement climatique, de la France à la Suède
france24fr.description: Les vendanges commencent cette semaine dans plusieurs vignobles français, environ trois semaines plus tôt que dans les années 1970. Une précocité exceptionnelle, symptôme d'un dérèglement climatique qui met la filière sous pression. Nouvelles techniques, nouveaux terroirs : le monde viticole riposte.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : la Banque mondiale accorde un prêt de 340 milliards de FCFA
france24fr.description: Le Sénégal obtient un financement de 340 milliards de francs CFA de la Banque mondiale. Un soutien qui marque un tournant après des mois de tensions avec les bailleurs internationaux, sur fond de controverse autour de la dette cachée.

france24fr.title: Salle de bal à la Maison Blanche : Trump fulmine après un nouveau revers en appel
france24fr.description: La construction à la Maison Blanche de la controversée salle de bal voulue par Donald Trump a été bloquée vendredi par une cour d'appel fédérale. La juridiction maintient la suspension des travaux ordonnée en avril par un juge. Dénonçant une décision "horrible" et "politique", le président américain a annoncé saisir la Cour suprême.

france24fr.title: Syrie : l'explosion d'un bus fait 14 blessés à Jaramana, près de Damas
france24fr.description: Quatorze personnes ont été blessées, dont trois sont dans un état critique, lors d'une explosion dans un bus de transport de passagers à Jaramana, près de Damas. Une enquête a été ouverte pour établir les circonstances de l'attentat et en identifier les responsables. Depuis la chute de Bachar al-Assad, la Syrie est le théâtre d'attaques sporadiques visant des civils et les forces de sécurité.

france24fr.title: Rwanda : une nouvelle génération de cinéastes à l'honneur
france24fr.description: À Kigali, le cinéma rwandais connaît une nouvelle effervescence. Plusieurs salles ont été réhabilitées et des projections en plein air ont été organisées ces dernières semaines, témoignant d’un regain d’intérêt pour le septième art dans la capitale. Reportage d'Aurore Bayoud.

france24fr.title: Afrique du Sud : le départ des migrants met des usines à l’arrêt
france24fr.description: En Afrique du Sud, plusieurs usines tournent au ralenti, voire sont à l’arrêt, après le départ de nombreux travailleurs migrants. À Newcastle, dans la province du KwaZulu-Natal, des postes restent vacants dans l’industrie textile, à la suite de plusieurs semaines de manifestations visant les étrangers. Récit de Laurent Berstecher.

zeit.title: Unfälle: Motorradfahrerin bei Unfall nahe Venningen schwer verletzt
Fußball: UEFA bestätigt Zahlungen an Ex-Mitarbeiterin von Infantino
Marode Brücke: Bagger rücken an: Abriss an Bonner Nordbrücke hat begonnen
Manöver in Taiwan: Taiwans Präsident Lai überwacht Großmanöver des Militärs
zeit.description: Wegen drohender Angriffe aus China führt Taiwan militärische Manöver durch, um seine Abwehr zu testen. Präsident Lai überwachte den Einsatz von Angriffsdrohnen. ​

zeit.title: Fußball-Bundesliga: Bayer-Boss Carro: «Bundesliga braucht dringend Abwechslung»
Wetter: Hochsommerliches Wochenende - doch Regen ist in Sicht
Kriminalität: Schuss bei Streit vor Bielefelder Hauptbahnhof gefallen
Kolumbien: Abelardo de la Espriella als neuer Präsident Kolumbiens vereidigt
zeit.description: In Kolumbien hat der rechte Hardliner Abelardo de la Espriella offiziell das Amt des Präsidenten übernommen. Er will unter anderem hart gegen Drogengewalt vorgehen.

zeit.title: Techunternehmen: EU-Kommissarin gibt TikTok und Meta Mitschuld an Krise in Ceuta
zeit.description: Auf TikTok und Facebook hätten sich Falschinformationen zur Situation in Ceuta verbreitet, sagt Henna Virkkunen. Die Unternehmen hätten stärker dagegen vorgehen müssen.

zeit.title: Wetterprognose: Bis 36 Grad - Gewitter und Sturmböen im Bergland möglich
Notfälle: Motorboot läuft mit Wasser voll - Besatzung gerettet
UCLA-Experiment: Die Erotik der Murmeltiere
zeit.description: Weil Trump einer biologischen Fakultät die Mittel kürzt, müssen Nagetiere jetzt bei OnlyFans anschaffen gehen. Dabei würde unser Autor viel lieber mal mit ihnen reden.

zeit.title: Badegewässer: Parasiten und Blaualgen lieben heißes Wetter
zeit.description: Parasiten, Blaualgen: Will man wirklich wissen, was da mit einem im Wasser schwimmt? Frau Jarosch will. Wir haben sie bei einem Kontrollgang begleitet.

zeit.title: Lebenssinn: Kann man Sinn verlernen?
zeit.description: Stress, Routinen und Lebensumbrüche verdecken manchmal, was uns wichtig ist. Strategien aus der Psychologie können helfen, es wieder freizulegen.

zeit.title: Lkw-Fahrverbot an Sonntagen: BUND kritisiert Lockerung des Sonntagsfahrverbots für Lkw
zeit.description: Wegen niedriger Flussstände ist der Transport von Gütern per Schiff derzeit eingeschränkt. Den Vorschlag, deshalb auch sonntags Lkw fahren zu lassen, kritisiert der BUND.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Migrantenansturm in Ceuta: Spanien führt Grenzkontrollen für Reisende aus Italien ein
nzz.description: Die Lage in der spanischen Exklave Ceuta in Nordafrika ist nach der Ankunft Tausender Migranten angespannt. Die neusten Meldungen zur Migrationskrise.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Tote nach Luftangriffen auf Vorort von Kiew +++ Selenski dankt US-Senat für Russland-Sanktionen
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: Linke und Bürgerliche kritisieren die Reservekraftwerke des Bundesrates und fordern einen Planungsstopp
nzz.description: Für 2,3 Milliarden Franken will der Energieminister fünf neue Reservekraftwerke bauen und so die Versorgungssicherheit der Schweiz langfristig absichern, doch im Parlament haben immer mehr Politiker Zweifel und fordern ein Umdenken.

nzz.title: «In den USA geht die Post ab»: Trotz enttäuschender Aktie verteidigt der Amrize-Chef Jan Jenisch die Abspaltung von Holcim
nzz.description: Das frühere Nordamerika-Geschäft von Holcim wächst schnell, aber nicht an der Börse. Donald Trump macht dem Zementkonzern das Leben schwer.

nzz.title: Xi Jinpings engster Vertrauter: Cai Qi, der Strippenzieher hinter den Kulissen
nzz.description: Derzeit entspannt sich Chinas Parteielite in dem mondänen Seebad Beidaihe. Auch dort dürfte Cai Qi kaum von der Seite seines Chefs weichen. Wer ist der Mann hinter Xi Jinping?

nzz.title: Diese Badi ist eine Zumutung: Die Rohre rosten, die Anlagen sind marode, die Google-Bewertungen – eine Katastrophe. Aber Guido Scherer will sie retten. Warum?
nzz.description: Von der Unmöglichkeit, eine Badi zu sanieren. Und von der grösseren Unmöglichkeit, sie für die Zukunft zu retten.

nzz.title: Gehen den USA im Iran-Krieg die Abwehr- und Präzisionsraketen aus? Donald Trump bestreitet jegliche Engpässe
nzz.description: Um amerikanische Truppen möglichst nicht in Gefahr zu bringen, liess Donald Trump Iran aus der Ferne bombardieren. Nun sind die Bestände an amerikanischen Präzisionsraketen gesunken – mit Folgen über Iran hinaus.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Wir wollen Krieg gegen das Feuer führen, doch dieser Krieg ist verloren, bevor er überhaupt begonnen hat»
nzz.description: Die französische Philosophin Joëlle Zask beschäftigt sich mit den Gefahren durch Waldbrände, die so extrem sind, dass sie kaum mehr zu löschen sind. Im Interview erklärt sie, welche Abwehrmittel den Menschen bleiben.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Der Drohnenangriff am Flughafen Leipzig kam mit Ansage. Europa muss endlich die Zeichen sehen
nzz.description: Russland lässt den Konflikt mit dem Westen seit einiger Zeit eskalieren. Dass Drohnen dabei eine Rolle spielen, ist bekannt. Dennoch wird die Bedrohung weitherum ignoriert. Das ist gefährlich.

nzz.title: Selenski ist erstmals in Serbien willkommen: Belgrad vollzieht einen Tabubruch
nzz.description: Hinter der Einladung des prorussischen serbischen Präsidenten Aleksandar Vucic stehen strategische Eigeninteressen. Für Moskau ist der Besuch ein Rückschlag.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - «Fiskalische Fussfessel»: Javier Mileis Ideen zur Schuldenbegrenzung täten auch den USA oder Frankreich gut
nzz.description: Der argentinische Präsident will die notorische Schuldenpolitik in seinem Land beenden. Neue Regeln braucht es auch im hochverschuldeten Westen.

nzz.title: Migranten dringen durch selbstgebaute Tunnel in Litauen ein und attackieren Grenzbeamte – zeitgleich warnt der Geheimdienst vor einer russischen False-Flag-Operation
nzz.description: Mit instrumentalisierter Migration will der weissrussische Autokrat Alexander Lukaschenko Chaos stiften. Während die Aufmerksamkeit an die Grenze gelenkt wird, plant der Kreml möglicherweise schon die nächste Provokation.

nzz.title: Der umtriebige Michele Maggi: Wie ein politischer Flüchtling den Grundstein für eine Weltmarke legte
nzz.description: Er flüchtete aus dem reaktionären Italien und hatte in der Schweiz als Unternehmer Erfolg. Nur so konnte sein verhaltensauffälliger Sohn Julius das Maggi-Imperium aufbauen. Dies zeigen neue Archivfunde.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Die Idee, dass jeder Mensch, der die europäische Grenze erreicht, ein Asylverfahren erhält, ist überholt», sagt der Asyljurist Daniel Thym nach der Ceuta-Krise
nzz.description: Die Ceuta-Krise befeuert die europäische Asyldebatte. Europäische Politiker möchten die Asylverfahren an Drittstaaten auslagern. Daniel Thym hält das für illusorisch. An den Gerichten führe kein Weg vorbei.

nzz.title: Eine Woche Ausnahmezustand in Ceuta – so lief die beispiellose Massenabschiebung nach dem Ansturm ab
nzz.description: In den letzten Julitagen rennen 70 000 Migranten los, um Spanien zu erreichen. Die Grenze kollabiert. 48 Stunden später sind fast alle zurückgekehrt. Wie ist das so schnell gelungen?

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - «Ich habe mich vor einer Gruppe Touristen ausgeweint. Ich nenne es einen ‹taktischen Weinkrampf›.» Sophie Woods läuft die Via Alpina in Rekordzeit
nzz.description: 28 Tage braucht die Neuseeländerin für den 2000 Kilometer langen Fernwanderweg – dabei wollte sie nach missglückten Versuchen, schwanger zu werden, nur ihren Körper wieder lieben.

observador.title: Um filme tristonho sobre um cantor que espalhava alegria
observador.description: "Playback", de Sérgio Graciano, não presta um bom serviço a Carlos Paião, nem à memória do que ele significou para os portugueses nos inesquecíveis anos 80. Eurico de Barros dá-lhe uma estrela.

observador.title: Mais de 60 concelhos do país em perigo máximo de incêndio
observador.description: Mais de 60 concelhos do interior Norte e Centro e do Algarve estão hoje em perigo máximo de incêndio, segundo o Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera (IPMA).

observador.title: Kanye West no Estádio do Algarve: a arte de um homem sozinho
observador.description: Num dos poucos concertos não cancelados, entre fãs vindos do México ou da Maia, a pergunta que pairou foi uma só: pode a genialidade artística de Ye redimi-lo dos seus atos mais sombrios?

observador.title: Quercus alerta para impactos subavaliados de central eólica
observador.description: A Quercus manifestou preocupação com o projeto do Parque Eólico do Sudoeste, alertando para o que considera a subavaliação dos impactos ambientais da central para abastecer o centro de dados de Sines.

observador.title: Tufão Dolphin leva China a elevar nível de alerta
observador.description: Tufão Dolphin atinge Okinawa no Japão e deixa China em alerta com portos fechados e a navegação de ferries suspensa na costa leste. O nível de alerta laranja é o segundo mais grave.

observador.title: Barragens da EDP. PS questiona Governo sobre impostos
observador.description: Socialistas voltam a questionar ministro das Finanças sobre liquidação de impostos sobre a venda de barragens da EDP e o risco de caducarem. Prazo para cobrar termina em outubro.

observador.title: Três mortos em ataque russo contra Kiev
observador.description: A Rússia lançou mais ataques noturnos contra Kiev, matando três pessoas, incluindo uma criança de três anos. Há registo de sete feridos.

observador.title: As notícias das 9h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: "Agendódromo". A investigação que leva Luís Neves a tribunal
observador.description: As suspeitas de corrupção no consulado de Portugal no Rio de Janeiro e o envolvimento do Primeiro Comando da Capital levaram 23 elementos da PJ ao Brasil. São as viagens que ditam o julgamento no TdC.

observador.title: 8h. PS questiona sobre risco de caducidade nas barragens
observador.description: O PS quer saber se há risco de caducarem 335 milhões em impostos das barragens da EDP. Miguel Costa Matos questiona o Governo sobre o atraso no fundo para as populações locais.

observador.title: Desenhar o mundo
observador.description: O geógrafo Miguel Antunes começou a viajar tarde, em 2013. Nesse ano, redescobriu a paixão pelo desenho e desde então tem viajado e desenhado nas mais diversas geografias.

observador.title: 7h. Seguro envia "Lei do Retorno" ao Constitucional
observador.description: O Presidente António José Seguro enviou a lei do retorno ao Constitucional por dúvidas sobre a detenção de imigrantes. Deu luz verde à prestação social única, mas avisa: ninguém pode ser prejudicado.

observador.title: 6h. Sporting estreia-se hoje no campeonato frente ao Estrela
observador.description: Rui Borges fala numa deslocação complicada. Pepa garante foco na equipa. Ainda, Luís Neves esteve envolvido na decisão de avançar com as auditorias à Polícia Judiciária.

observador.title: Canções para o Eclipse
observador.description: Como soa o dia a escurecer? Do ecletismo dos Talking Heads e Yeah Yeah Yeahs à voz mística de Né Ladeiras e ao clássico dos Pink Floyd, desenhamos a banda sonora ideal para o eclipse.

observador.title: 4h. Dominado incêndio em Fornos de Algodres
observador.description: Fogo deflagrou a pouca distância de um outro incêndio que atingiu o concelho, em Vila Ruiva. Ainda, PJ confrontou diretor financeiro sobre ligação à Construbarcelos, mas afasta processo disciplinar

observador.title: 3h. Governo articulou auditorias à PJ com Luís Neves
observador.description: Investigações fazem parte da estratégia do Executivo para afastar suspeitas de proteção política e retirar força à CPI do Chega. Ainda nesta edição, Estoril e Famalicão abrem a época a empatar.

observador.title: 2h. Espanha restabelece controlos fronteiriços com Itália
observador.description: Decisão surge após Roma recusar levantar restrições a viajantes de Espanha, após a crise migratória em Ceuta. Ainda, PCP diz que decisão de Seguro sobre lei do retorno não é surpresa.

observador.title: 1h. Operacionais combatem incêndio em Fornos de Algodres
observador.description: Fogo tem apenas uma frente ativa. Chamas chegaram a aproximar-se das localidades de Vila Chã e Muxagata. Ainda neste jornal, Presidente da República remete lei do retorno para o Constitucional.

spiegel.title: Uganda: Parlament billigt Truppenentsendung in den Gazastreifen
spiegel.description: Donald Trump will den Gazakrieg mit seinem Friedensrat beenden. Nun hat das Gremium offenbar den ersten Bauauftrag erteilt – für eine Militärbasis im völlig zerstörten Rafah. Dort soll ein marokkanisches Expeditionskorps stationiert werden.

spiegel.title: USA: Generalstabschef Dan Caine sucht angeblich Ausweg aus Irankrieg
spiegel.description: Amerikas ranghöchster General glaubt offenbar nicht mehr an einen militärischen Sieg gegen Iran: Einem Bericht zufolge lotet Dan Caine derzeit aus, wie die USA sich zurückziehen könnten. Noch nicht eingeweiht: der Präsident.

spiegel.title: Griechenland: Deutscher Segler tot geborgen
spiegel.description: Er ging schwimmen, dann trieb das Boot ab: Ein deutscher Segler ist vor der Insel Symi in der Ägäis tot aufgefunden worden.

spiegel.title: Ohne Adresse: Innenministerium plant neuen Personalausweis
spiegel.description: Ein größeres Foto und keine aufgedruckte Anschrift mehr: Das Bundesinnenministerium arbeitet laut einem Zeitungsbericht an einem neuen Personalausweis.

spiegel.title: Südkorea: Fußballverband gibt Massage-Skandal zu
spiegel.description: Gleich mehrere Skandale erschüttern Südkoreas Fußballverband. Nun hat sich die KFA dafür entschuldigt, ausländischen Schiedsrichtern Sexmassagen spendiert zu haben. Die Organisation befinde sich »in einer desolaten Lage«.

spiegel.title: Armenien: Orthodoxes Kirchenoberhaupt Karekin II. steht vor Gericht
spiegel.description: Ein bislang einmaliger Vorgang in den Nachfolgestaaten der Sowjetunion: Armeniens orthodoxes Kirchenoberhaupt ist angeklagt. Der Grund: Karekin II. soll sich über das weltliche Gericht hinweggesetzt haben.

spiegel.title: Südostfrankreich: Ausbreitung von Waldbrand nach 18 Tagen gestoppt
spiegel.description: Er hat mehrere Ortschaften bedroht und Dutzende Häuser zerstört: Einsatzkräfte haben die Ausbreitung eines Waldbrands im Département Var eingedämmt.

spiegel.title: USA: Donald Trump wirft Kuba vor, als Operationsbasis für China, Russland und Iran zu dienen
spiegel.description: Donald Trump und Marco Rubio wollen das Regime in Havanna stürzen – auch mit Sanktionen. Die treffen nun auch die kubanischen Militärattachés an den Botschaften in Moskau und Peking.

spiegel.title: Nordkorea: Staatsmedien empfehlen Hundefleischsuppe gegen Hitzewelle
spiegel.description: 2027 tritt in Nordkorea ein Hundefleischverbot in Kraft. Aber weil es aktuell so heiß ist, gibt die Staatspresse Ernährungstipps, für die noch Vierbeiner gebraucht werden.

spiegel.title: Österreich: So drastisch wirkt sich die Hitze auf das Land aus
spiegel.description: Die Folgen der Klimakrise wirken sich zwischen Neusiedler See und Bodensee besonders drastisch aus. Die FPÖ reagiert besonders peinlich.

spiegel.title: Utah: Löschhubschrauber stürzt bei Waldbrand in den USA ab
spiegel.description: Beim Kampf gegen Waldbrände in Utah ist ein Löschhubschrauber verunglückt. Zum Zustand der zwei Insassen gibt es bislang keine Angaben. Einsatzkräfte versuchen, in den kommenden Stunden zur Absturzstelle vorzudringen.

spiegel.title: Rentenreform: Wirtschaftsweiser Werding fordert Abschaffung der Witwenrente
spiegel.description: Martin Werding will die Witwenrente durch ein Splitting ersetzen. Zugleich warnt der Wirtschaftsweise davor, die Reform wegen des Streits über die »Rente mit 63« aufzuschnüren.

spiegel.title: Tennis: Eva Lys spricht offen über Geldsorgen
spiegel.description: Lockt im Tennis das große Geld? Profispielerin Eva Lys hat jetzt in einem Interview erstaunlich offen darüber gesprochen, wie schwer es ist, in dem Sport zu bestehen. Und wie es war, den ersten dicken Scheck zu bekommen.

spiegel.title: Lars Klingbeil: SPD-Finanzminister plant offenbar stärkere Besteuerung von Vereinen

phys-org.title: Silver nanocatalysts switch reaction sites between power generation and hydrogen production
phys-org.description: For the first time, researchers have discovered that the same silver (Ag) nanocatalyst operates at different reaction sites depending on whether a solid oxide cell is generating electricity or producing hydrogen. This finding introduces a new design principle for improving the performance of next-generation solid oxide cells.

phys-org.title: One million years without sex fails to erase stick insects' unused biological system
phys-org.description: Scientists have made a surprising finding about how an asexually reproducing stick insect has evolved. Research led by Dr. Darren Parker, lecturer in evolutionary biology at Bangor University, studied the genes of several species of Timema (a type of stick insect), which have not engaged in sexual reproduction for 1 million years—the longest known asexual period for any insect.

phys-org.title: New AI model reveals the volume of the world's glaciers
phys-org.description: How much ice is stored in the world's glaciers? And where exactly is it located? A new study led by Ca' Foscari University of Venice, in collaboration with the Institute of Polar Sciences of the National Research Council of Italy (CNR-ISP), provides an updated global map of glacier ice volume.

phys-org.title: Creating cleaner chemical reactions that run on oxygen and produce only water as waste
phys-org.description: Oxygen provides the driving force for many vital chemical reactions. Two well-known examples include respiration, the process that allows living things to break down food to release its energy, and combustion, reactions that produce heat and light. But oxygen has an unusual electronic configuration that tends to slow reactions with organic matter, so reactions often need help to get started. In nature, specialized proteins called enzymes can activate oxygen on demand by first rearranging its ele

phys-org.title: Researchers unlock high-res view of 2D materials by doing a microscopic twist
phys-org.description: By rapidly twisting a microscopically small tip back and forth, researchers at the University of Maryland (UMD) have unlocked a new way to detect subtle changes on the surface of a material flexing in response to infrared light.

phys-org.title: Hidden anatomy of clouds reveals how rain may begin without ice crystals
phys-org.description: The initiation of rain in clouds without ice remains one of the largest unsolved mysteries in atmospheric science.

phys-org.title: Laser spectroscopy helps reveal hidden nuclear properties in fermium
phys-org.description: For the first time, researchers have determined the shape of the actinide nucleus of fermium-255 and measured its structure with high precision and resolution.

phys-org.title: New 'shape-shifting' architecture brings versatility to photonic quantum computing
phys-org.description: Using light to process quantum information is one of the most promising approaches to building future quantum computers. Light particles, known as photons, are excellent carriers of quantum information, but their lack of natural interactions has created a major challenge for researchers seeking to build systems capable of performing a full range of computations.

phys-org.title: Crossing into a mirror world: Particles turn to wisps of fog, and the magnetic monopole paradox dissolves
phys-org.description: In Goethe's ballad "Erlkönig," immortalized in Schubert's fevered 1815 setting, a dying boy riding through the night sees a spectral king beckoning from the darkness. His father calms him: "Mein Sohn, es ist ein Nebelstreif"—my son, it is only a wisp of fog. In the poem, the father's reassurance proves tragically wrong. In the quantum world, however, his words acquire an uncanny new meaning.

phys-org.title: Tiny floating magnet detects ultrafaint magnetic fields at room temperature
phys-org.description: Measuring faint magnetic fields is useful in a number of areas, including mapping brain activity, monitoring hearts and probing fundamental physics. Typically, picking up such weak signals requires expensive or bulky equipment, such as liquid-helium cooling tanks or specially shielded rooms that block out Earth's magnetic field.

phys-org.title: Antenna-like cell appendage may help turtle embryos sense sex-deciding nest temperatures
phys-org.description: When most baby turtles hatch, their sex depends on the temperature of the sand or soil where their mother laid her eggs. Warm incubation produces females, while cool nests produce males.

phys-org.title: Hydraulic traits reveal why some mountain trees move uphill while others shift downhill
phys-org.description: As global temperatures rise, scientists have largely assumed that mountain tree species will move uphill in search of cooler conditions. A new study published in Nature Climate Change reveals a more complex reality: Some tree species are moving uphill, while others are shifting downhill, and the key to understanding these contrasting responses lies in how trees manage water.

phys-org.title: Boron layers could set a superconductivity record, theoretical study predicts
phys-org.description: Scientists in China predict that stacking two microscopic layers of boron could set a new record for superconductivity. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with zero resistance. Traditional types need temperatures close to absolute zero to work, requiring complex and expensive cooling equipment.

phys-org.title: New platform speeds bacterial gene mapping for better biotech design
phys-org.description: Scientists at the Department of Energy's Oak Ridge National Laboratory have created a platform that pinpoints genetic triggers that turn microbes into efficient factories for new chemicals and materials. The method enables rapid, precise reprogramming of bacteria as biotechnology tools, supporting domestic production of valuable products and recovery of critical minerals and materials to enhance the nation's supply chains and global competitiveness.

phys-org.title: Mobile fungal 'Starship' carries protein that triggers crop leaf loss
phys-org.description: An international research team led by plant scientist Professor Dr. Bart Thomma of the Institute of Plant Sciences at the University of Cologne, the MiBiNet Collaborative Research Center and the CEPLAS Cluster of Excellence for Plant Sciences has identified the region of the genome in the pathogenic fungus Verticillium dahliae responsible for producing a specific protein that the pathogen secretes during infection.

phys-org.title: First full zoysia grass genetic blueprint opens doors for drought-tolerant turf
phys-org.description: A new genomic resource from the Texas A&M AgriLife Research plant genomics team is providing a powerful new foundation for faster, more precise turfgrass genetics and breeding. The team discovered a breakthrough genome that finally reveals the full genetic blueprint of zoysia grass.

phys-org.title: The creatures born from code: Generative AI threatens to upend citizen science records
phys-org.description: You need to tread carefully among the leaf litter of the Indonesian scrubland and its tropical rainforests. The dead leaves might seem caught in a gentle breeze, but there's more here than meets the eye. Try plucking one from the ground and you'll find an insect caught in the act of prayer.

phys-org.title: Hidden hormone–habitat relationship revealed in reef fish
phys-org.description: In the animal kingdom, only those that adapt to their environment survive. This adaptation takes a wide range of forms, from invisible internal shifts in gene expression to dramatic anatomical changes, such as tadpoles growing legs and transitioning to life on land as frogs.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: The Ceuta Crisis Is About More Than Migration
proj-syn.description: When tens of thousands of people recently entered the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from neighboring Morocco, European leaders lapsed into recriminations, reigniting the debate on migration. But the bigger challenge is to address a long-simmering territorial dispute between Spain and Morocco.

proj-syn.title: The Rising Price of a Cheap Renminbi
proj-syn.description: Renminbi appreciation would not, on its own, rebalance China’s economy and eliminate its massive surpluses. But by increasing households’ purchasing power over imports and compressing tradable-sector margins, it would raise the cost of avoiding reform.

proj-syn.title: Who Should Build the Low-Carbon Economy?
proj-syn.description: Since the first Industrial Revolution, goods and technologies have reached the farthest corners of the world, but the ability to design, build, market, and extract value from them has remained highly concentrated. Unless humanity can break this pattern, a sufficient response to climate change will remain out of reach.

proj-syn.title: Will Iceland Rejoin the EU Path?
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s volatile and unpredictable security policies, particularly his desire to control Greenland, have put Iceland in a vulnerable position. This uncomfortable reality will likely be front of mind as voters decide whether to reopen membership negotiations with the European Union.

proj-syn.title: Democracy, Autocracy, or Something Else?
proj-syn.description: Contrary to conventional wisdom, the world is neither converging on liberal democracy nor being swept by an authoritarian tide. The decisive political struggles of the 21st century will be won or lost through the unglamorous work of strengthening democratic accountability and building effective institutions.

proj-syn.title: Colombia’s New Right-Wing Government Faces an Uphill Battle
proj-syn.description: Colombian President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella inherits an economy constrained by weak investment and a severe fiscal crisis. His ability to restore fiscal stability without sacrificing the social gains of recent decades will determine whether the country’s rightward shift proves lasting or short-lived.

proj-syn.title: Can Progressives Deliver Economic Growth?
proj-syn.description: At a time of historic inequality and inadequate public investment, the kind of redistributive policies promoted by politicians on the left are badly needed. But given that no jurisdiction can tax and regulate its way to affordability, a growth-enhancing agenda that generates good jobs and productive capacity is also vital.

proj-syn.title: Fauci’s Modern Pillory
proj-syn.description: MAGA Republicans’ decision to drag Anthony Fauci before a Senate hearing was less about their hatred of science and more about their disdain for the scientists who guide lawmakers in their decision-making. They couldn’t wait to pillory him, and by association any public-facing expert, in front of the cameras.

proj-syn.title: Cheaper Mortgages Won’t Solve the US Housing Crisis
proj-syn.description: For decades, federal housing policy has favored cheaper financing over expanding the housing supply, despite evidence that expanding mortgage credit increases borrowing and house prices. The bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act marks an important shift by emphasizing measures that make it easier to build more homes.

proj-syn.title: The Right Way to Regulate AI
proj-syn.description: Governments tend to treat AI as a national-security challenge while devoting far less attention to its effects on education, health, labor markets, and the judiciary. Addressing AI’s societal risks requires institutions designed to recognize and respond to emerging threats before they become systemic failures.

proj-syn.title: Global Tax Reform Is the Key to a Fair AI Economy
proj-syn.description: The rise of AI has highlighted how the global tax system is ill-suited to capture the profits derived from such technology. While creating an equitable AI economy ultimately requires a durable and robust multilateral tax framework, digital-service taxes can serve as an important stepping stone to that outcome.

proj-syn.title: Aid’s Next Chapter
proj-syn.description: Wars, epidemics, displacement, and geopolitical competition will ensure that rich countries continue to spend money abroad, whether for humanitarian reasons or in pursuit of their own interests. The only question is what sort of aid system will emerge from the current retrenchment.

proj-syn.title: Peace With Iran Won’t Last Unless It Benefits Ordinary Iranians
proj-syn.description: A sustainable peace agreement between the United States and Iran will require more than military deterrence. Without financial sanctions relief that fuels job creation and generates real economic opportunities for ordinary Iranians, it will likely suffer the same fate as the 2015 nuclear deal.

proj-syn.title: Why Wealth Taxes Always Fail
proj-syn.description: A clear-eyed view of past experience shows that where wealth taxes have been tried, they have usually been abandoned—and for good reason. As policymakers in California, New York, France, and elsewhere revisit this old idea, they should heed the lessons of this history.

proj-syn.title: A New Paradigm for Global Health Financing
proj-syn.description: As aid flows decline, more countries are articulating a new vision in which health financing would build on national resources, answer to domestic priorities, and remain accountable to their own citizens. Such a change is long overdue, and it can be achieved by pursuing reforms in three areas.

proj-syn.title: The Triumph of India’s Cockroaches
proj-syn.description: The concessions secured by the "cockroach movement" amount to more than a triumph for prospective medical students or a brief political headache for the country's ruling party. They prove that even after years of centralization and institutional erosion, power remains with the people.

proj-syn.title: Zombie Monetarism
proj-syn.description: Three prominent economists, including a former Federal Reserve governor and adviser to US President Donald Trump, have just endorsed “soft monetarism” as a way to guide the Fed's approach to inflation. But the "quantity theory" of money failed for good reasons, and those reasons have not changed.

proj-syn.title: Taiwan Needs a New Deterrence Strategy

To avert a Chinese invasion, Taiwan must ensure that other democracies cannot function without it by providing them with more than just semiconductors.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: A Big Week For Big Checks
crunchbase.description: Startups raised funding rounds with a lot of zeroes at the end this week, with three companies securing financings of $1 billion or more. Additionally, a robust lineup of companies in sectors including AI, e-commerce, cybersecurity, biotech and even mining also announced sizable new rounds.

crunchbase.description: Active startup investors kept up the pace in July, with familiar names topping the ranks in several metrics including most prolific venture dealmakers, most active lead backers, biggest spenders and highest-volume seed investors.

crunchbase.title: The Return Of The Repeat Founder: Inside YC’s Growing Class Of Second-Timers
crunchbase.description: We analyzed a dataset of repeat founders who have gone through Y Combinator’s cohorts and found some very interesting insights. The dataset, shared with us directly from YC, consisted of 454 repeat founders through the program as well as 935 founder-company records spanning 2005 through 2026. We spoke to a couple of them about their experiences.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
crunchbase.description: Over 127,000 workers at U.S.-based tech companies were laid off in mass job cuts in 2025, per a Crunchbase News tally, and the layoffs have continued into 2026. See the latest companies to cut roles.

crunchbase.title: ‘Nobody Wanted to Give A Former Principal Money’: How An Educator Built An Edtech AI Startup With $63M From VCs
crunchbase.description: Founded by an educator fascinated by the educational potential of ChatGPT, MagicSchool AI leads off a series of articles featuring startup founders from non-technical backgrounds who have launched successful venture-backed companies.

crunchbase.title: Your AI Strategy May Be Destroying Your Exit Value
crunchbase.description: While integrating AI into a startup's product strategy is often viewed as a way to enhance valuation, it can inadvertently reduce exit value, argues tech strategic adviser Itay Sagie. In this guest commentary he shares three ways your AI strategy can provide a positive impact on valuation when it becomes time for an exit.

crunchbase.title: A Record 14 Billion-Dollar Rounds In July Pushed Venture’s Historic Run Higher
crunchbase.description: Global venture funding showed no signs of slowing in July. Startup capital totaled $65 billion, up 100% year over year, as the month notched the highest-ever number of billion-dollar venture rounds on record, per Crunchbase data.

crunchbase.title: Why The Product Manager To CEO Pipeline Is The Underrated Crash Course For Leadership In Tech
crunchbase.description: Traditional research on CEO career paths tends to focus on titles such as COO, CFO and divisional president. But the skills developed in product management may be just as relevant, argues Paysend CEO Ben Chisell. In this guest column, he makes the case that aspiring leaders should focus less on collecting prestigious titles and more on taking ownership of measurable business outcomes.

crunchbase.title: ‘A Rare Land-Grab Moment’: Menlo Ventures’ Matt Murphy On The Next Wave of AI And Putting $3B In New Capital To Work
crunchbase.description: We speak with Menlo Ventures' Matt Murphy about why AI is pushing the firm toward larger deals, what it has learned from its Anthropic relationship, and where he sees the next big opportunities.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Safe Superintelligence And Commonwealth Fusion Lead With Billion-Dollar Deals
crunchbase.description: Another week, another bevy of big rounds. The largest round was a reported $5 billion Nvidia-backed financing for foundational AI unicorn Safe Superintelligence, followed by a $1 billion investment in Commonwealth Fusion Systems.
